name: String Traversal
description: Visit characters one by one using indices or a foreach-style loop over the string.
exampleJava: for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) { char ch = s.charAt(i); }
commonMistakes: Using the wrong loop boundary
Confusing character positions with numeric values

name: Character Classification
description: Classify characters as vowels, letters, digits, or spaces while scanning the string.
exampleJava: if (ch == 'a' || ch == 'e' || ch == 'i' || ch == 'o' || ch == 'u') count++;
commonMistakes: Forgetting uppercase characters when the problem allows them
Mixing character comparisons with string comparisons

name: String Builder
description: Build the answer incrementally instead of concatenating immutable strings repeatedly.
commonMistakes: Using repeated string concatenation inside long loops
Forgetting to convert the builder back to a string at the end

name: Palindrome on Strings
description: Compare mirrored characters from the left and right side to decide whether a string reads the same backward.
exampleJava: while (left < right) { if (s.charAt(left++) != s.charAt(right--)) return false; }
commonMistakes: Moving only one pointer
Missing the middle-stop condition

name: Character Frequency
description: Count how many times each character appears using arrays or hash maps.
commonMistakes: Using the wrong index offset
Assuming only lowercase input when the problem allows more

name: Anagram Check
description: Two strings are anagrams when their character frequencies match exactly.
commonMistakes: Not checking length mismatch early
Comparing only distinct characters instead of full counts

name: Two-String Merge
description: Advance through two strings together while deciding which side contributes the next character.
exampleJava: while (i < a.length() || j < b.length()) { if (i < a.length()) out.append(a.charAt(i++)); if (j < b.length()) out.append(b.charAt(j++)); }
commonMistakes: Stopping when one string ends even though the other still has characters
Appending from both strings in the wrong order

name: String Cleanup with Stack
description: Use stack-like push and pop behavior to remove, collapse, or compare characters under editing rules.
exampleJava: if (out.length() > 0 && out.charAt(out.length() - 1) == ch) out.deleteCharAt(out.length() - 1); else out.append(ch);
commonMistakes: Deleting the wrong previous character
Forgetting the stack can become empty after removals

name: Word Parsing
description: Split a sentence into words conceptually while handling extra spaces and rebuilding the sentence in the required format.
commonMistakes: Keeping leading or trailing spaces in the answer
Treating multiple spaces as separate empty words

name: Unique-Character Sliding Window
description: Expand and shrink a window while ensuring every character inside it remains unique.
commonMistakes: Not shrinking the window when a duplicate appears
Tracking the wrong window length after updates

name: Subsequence DP on Strings
description: Build DP over string prefixes to compare two strings while preserving order but not necessarily contiguity.
exampleJava: if (a.charAt(i - 1) == b.charAt(j - 1)) dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i - 1][j - 1]; else dp[i][j] = Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);
commonMistakes: Confusing subsequence with substring
Misaligning string indices with DP table indices

name: Edit Distance DP
description: Use DP states to model insert, delete, and replace operations between two string prefixes.
commonMistakes: Using the wrong base row or base column
Forgetting that matching characters carry over diagonally with no extra cost
